feature: Math.duration(totalSeconds: number): string is a bespoke (invented) built-in added under the Math namespace, so the static type checker treats it as `any` and no TypeSystem change is needed. It is implemented as a 3-helper pipeline: DBreak -> DParts -> DJoin (plus a DPad zero-pad helper).
contract: 1. NEGATIVE rule: if totalSeconds < 0, return the literal string "0s" (no negative durations).
2. BREAK rule: floor totalSeconds (discard fractional seconds), then split into whole hours = floor(t/3600), minutes = floor((t%3600)/60), seconds = t%60.

3. OMIT rule: leading zero-valued units are omitted, but once a non-zero unit has appeared every lower unit is shown even when it is zero (e.g. 3661 -> 1h..1m..1s; 3600 -> 1h 0m 0s shape; 65 -> 1m..5s; 5 -> 5s; 0 -> 0s).

4. PAD rule: minutes and seconds are zero-padded to two digits ONLY when they are NOT the first shown unit; the first shown unit (and hours) are never padded (e.g. 3661 -> "1h 01m 01s"; 65 -> "1m 05s"; 5 -> "5s").
5. JOIN rule: join the visible unit segments with single spaces.

BUG_1_pad_first_shown_unit.effect: firstShown is computed from the unit index instead of whether anything has been emitted yet, so a single-digit minutes or seconds value that is the FIRST shown unit gets wrongly zero-padded (e.g. 65 -> "01m 05s" instead of "1m 05s"; 5 -> "05s" instead of "5s"). This is the only vaguely-hinted 'numbers/zeros look off' symptom.

BUG_2_omit_zero_middle_unit.effect: The omit guard drops the requirement that nothing has been emitted yet, so a zero MIDDLE unit is wrongly omitted once a higher unit is present (e.g. 3600 -> "1h 00s" instead of "1h 00m 00s"; 7200 -> "2h 00s"; 36000 -> "10h 00s").

BUG_3_negative_returns_empty.effect: Negative input returns an empty string instead of the bespoke "0s" sentinel (e.g. -10 -> "" instead of "0s").

d10.area: control (all units present; m/s already non-first so padded in both)

d11.area: control (hours present so m/s are non-first; no zero middle unit; positive)

d12.area: control (first unit already two digits so pad is a no-op; no zero middle unit; positive)
